Q: How to build the Apache Tomcat Native Library? A:

install dev tools

sudo apt install build-essential libapr1-dev libssl-dev -y

Prepare work dir under your Downloads directory

mkdir -p ~/Downloads/wk-000

Download Tomcat 9

cd ~/Downloads/wk-000

wget https://dlcdn.apache.org/tomcat/tomcat-9/v9.0.113/bin/apache-tomcat-9.0.113.tar.gz

Unzip Tomcat 9

tar -zxvf apache-tomcat-9.0.113.tar.gz

Unzip Tomcat Native Source

You don't need to download the Tomcat native source code separately; it's already included in the Tomcat bin directory.

cd ~/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/bin

tar -zxvf tomcat-native.tar.gz

Run Command configure

note: change /home/demo to your user directory path.

cd ~/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/bin/tomcat-native-1.3.1-src/native

./configure --with-apr=/usr/bin/apr-1-config \
            --with-java-home=$JAVA_HOME \
            --with-ssl=/usr \
            --prefix=/home/demo/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113

Run Command make and install

make

make install

If everything ok , you will see the message:

Libraries have been installed in:
   /home/demo/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/lib

Add setenv.sh

nano ~/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/bin/setenv.sh

Add two lines

CATALINA_OPTS="$CATALINA_OPTS -Djava.library.path=/home/demo/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/lib"

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:/home/demo/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/lib

make setenv.sh as executeable

chmod +x ~/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/bin/setenv.sh

Start tomcat

cd ~/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/bin
./startup.sh

Verify

Run Command 1: (under ~/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/bin )

grep -E "Native|APR" ../logs/catalina.out

If suceess, you will see:

20-Jan-2026 14:10:02.625 INFO [main] org.apache.catalina.core.AprLifecycleListener.lifecycleEvent Loaded Apache Tomcat Native library [1.3.1] using APR version [1.7.2].

Run Command 2: (under ~/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/bin )

grep "OpenSSL" ../logs/catalina.out

If suceess, you will see:

20-Jan-2026 14:10:02.626 INFO [main] org.apache.catalina.core.AprLifecycleListener.lifecycleEvent APR/OpenSSL configuration: useAprConnector [false], useOpenSSL [true]
20-Jan-2026 14:10:02.629 INFO [main] org.apache.catalina.core.AprLifecycleListener.initializeSSL OpenSSL successfully initialized [OpenSSL 3.0.13 30 Jan 2024]

Clean tomcat-native directory

rm -rf ~/Downloads/wk-000/apache-tomcat-9.0.113/bin/tomcat-native-1.3.1-src

The test and verification have now been successful. If you want to move the apache-tomcat-9.0.113 directory to another directory, please remember to adjust the directory path settings in apache-tomcat-9.0.113/bin/setenv.sh.

Q: Lightweight test management for tracking manual + automated test runs without heavy overhead? A:

For teams like the one you describe, I usually prioritize a few boring but important things over feature depth.

Speed and friction are number one. If logging a run, adding notes, or linking it to a build takes more than a few seconds, people stop doing it consistently. That is usually what kills adoption long term, not missing advanced reports. Fast navigation and responsive run history matter way more than people expect once the data grows.

The second thing is how well the tool supports partial truth. Exploratory notes, inconclusive results, known gaps, and “we did not test this yet” signals are just as important as pass or fail. Tools that force everything into rigid statuses tend to give a false sense of confidence. That is where lighter setups, including what you noticed with Tuskr, often work better than heavier platforms like TestRail or Qase for smaller teams.

Long term, I look for clarity over control. Can someone new quickly understand what was tested, why it was tested, and what risk was accepted for a given build. If the tool helps answer those questions without dictating process, it usually holds up. Feature lists rarely predict that.
